title: Simultaneous special and generic norm-pair interpolation
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $A$ an integral finite-type $k$-algebra, $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $K=\operatorname{Frac}A$, and $s$ a closed point with nonzero maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_s$. Let $p:Y\to U$ be a surjective H-projective morphism with $Y$ integral of finite type over $k$, all geometric fibres pure of dimension one, and $C=Y_K$ smooth and geometrically integral. Fix a closed immersion $i:Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^D_U$ and $L=i^*\mathcal O(1)$. Let a finite group $G$ act on $Y$ over $U$, faithfully on $C$. Put $B=\bigotimes_{g\in G}g^*L$ and use the norm sections $\mathcal N_G$ of [def-sfb-pencil-orbit-bundle-norm]. There exist an affine open neighbourhood $U'\subseteq U$ of $s$, an integer $n\geq1$, and ordinary sections $a,b\in\Gamma(Y_{U'},L^{\otimes n})$ with both of the following properties. On $Y_s$ the pair $\mathcal N_G(a_s),\mathcal N_G(b_s)$ generates $B_s^{\otimes n}$ and defines a finite morphism $Y_s\to\mathbf P^1_{\kappa(s)}$. On $C$ the pair $\mathcal N_G(a_K),\mathcal N_G(b_K)$ generates $B_K^{\otimes n}$ and defines a finite surjective morphism $C\to\mathbf P^1_K$ that is etale on a nonempty open. No infinitude of $k$ or $\kappa(s)$ and no condition on $\operatorname{char}k$ relative to $|G|$ is assumed.

The notions used are [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-kun-projective], [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-sc-invertible-module], [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf], [def-pc-scheme-fibre], [def-pc-base-change], [def-weil-pure-dimension], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections], [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism], [def-weil-etale-morphism].

proof.text: The morphism $p$ is proper by projective-implies-proper, and $U$ is Noetherian by finite-type-over-Noetherian applied to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ (a field has only the ideals $0$ and $k$). Let $\eta$ be the generic point of $U$, so $\kappa(\eta)=K$ and $Y_\eta=C$. For $j\in\{s,\eta\}$ base-change the specified embedding along $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(j)\to U$: by closed-immersion base change, $i_j:Y_j\to\mathbf P^D_U\times_U\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(j)=\mathbf P^D_{\kappa(j)}$ is a closed immersion (the equality is associativity of the fibre products defining projective space), so $Y_s$ and $C$ are projective over $\kappa(s)$ and $K$. Both $L_j=L|_{Y_j}$ and $i_j^*\mathcal O(1)$ are pullbacks of $\mathcal O(1)$ along the same composite, so the composition isomorphism of invertible-pullback-tensor (2) identifies them. Hence $L_s,L_K=L_\eta$ are ample and invertible by projective-ample-invertible. The scheme $Y_s$ is nonempty by surjectivity. The finite-type algebra dimension equality under field extension, applied on affine charts to the algebraic closures of $\kappa(s)$ and $K$, shows that $\dim Y_s=\dim C=1$: the nonempty geometric fibres are pure of dimension one. Thus the special-fibre pencil lemma applies without reducedness, and the generic separating-open lemma applies to the given smooth geometrically integral $C$ and faithful $G$-action.

proof.text: Choose $d\geq1$ and $u,v\in\Gamma(Y_s,L_s^{\otimes d})$ from ample-curve-two-section-pencil. Their norms generate $B_s^{\otimes d}$ and give a finite map $f_s:Y_s\to\mathbf P^1_{\kappa(s)}$. Let $n_0$ be the bound of separating-pair-open for $(C,G,L_K)$, and $d_0$ the bound of ample-fibre-section-lifting for $(p,L,s)$. Choose $r\geq1$ with $n=dr\geq\max(n_0,d_0,1)$. Let $V=\Gamma(C,L_K^{\otimes n})$ and take the nonempty open $W_n\subseteq V\times V$ supplied by separating-pair-open. The latter node expressly gives finite dimensionality of $V$ and all the generic norm-pencil conclusions for a point of $W_n(K)$.

proof.text: The pair $u^{\otimes r},v^{\otimes r}$ has norms $\mathcal N_G(u)^{\otimes r},\mathcal N_G(v)^{\otimes r}$. To check the comparisons in the current norm definition, trivialize all $g^*L_s$ on a common open and write $g^*u=f_g e_g^{\otimes d}$. Pullback-tensor compatibility and the defining permutation identify both norm sections with $(\prod_g f_g)^r(\bigotimes_g e_g)^{\otimes dr}$; the same calculation applies to $v$. It still generates $B_s^{\otimes n}$: locally wherever one original norm is a basis, its $r$-th power is a basis. Its morphism is $h_r\circ f_s$, where $h_r([x:y])=[x^r:y^r]$, as follows by the coordinate ratios on the two standard charts. Here is a direct finiteness check, including inseparable $r$. On either target chart, the inverse image under $h_r\circ f_s$ equals the inverse image under $f_s$ of that same chart, hence is affine, say $\operatorname{Spec}R$. Write $z$ for the original chart coordinate. If $e_1,\ldots,e_q$ generate $R$ over $\kappa(s)[z]$, then $z^j e_i$ with $0\leq j<r$ generate $R$ over $\kappa(s)[t]$, where $t$ acts as $z^r$. Finite-local-on-target now proves the powered morphism finite. This argument uses only the existing finite map and explicit module generators.

proof.text: Since $n\geq d_0$, apply ample-fibre-section-lifting separately to $u^{\otimes r}$ and $v^{\otimes r}$ and intersect the two resulting neighbourhoods. Choose a principal affine neighbourhood $U'=D(q)$ of $s$ inside that intersection, with $q\notin\mathfrak m_s$, and restrict the lifts to obtain $a_0,b_0\in M=\Gamma(Y_{U'},L^{\otimes n})$. Put $A'=A_q$; its fraction field is still $K$. The prescribed special restrictions of $a_0,b_0$ are exactly the powered pair in Step 3. Only two section lifts are needed, so their neighbourhoods can be intersected.

source.place: Tag 0D2M, lemma-ample-on-fibre, final surjectivity assertion with F = O_Y; representatives of the two germs

proof.text: The restricted $L^{\otimes n}$ is invertible and therefore quasi-coherent: locally trivializing $L$ also trivializes its tensor powers. The morphism $Y_{U'}\to\operatorname{Spec}A'$ is projective, hence proper. By the proper-morphism definition it is separated and of finite type; the finite-type definition gives quasi-compactness over the affine base. Fraction-field-sections-base-change therefore gives the canonical isomorphism $K\otimes_{A'}M\simeq\Gamma(C,g^*L^{\otimes n})=V$, the last identification $g^*(L^{\otimes n})\cong L_K^{\otimes n}$ by iterating the tensor isomorphism of invertible-pullback-tensor (2), carrying $1\otimes h$ to $h_K$. In particular the restrictions of elements of $M$ span $V$. Since $V$ is finite dimensional, choose $h_1,\ldots,h_e\in M$ whose restrictions form a $K$-basis. Indeed a finite spanning subfamily can be extracted from expressions for a basis of $V$ as finite linear combinations of restrictions, and a basis can then be extracted from that finite spanning subfamily. No freeness or flatness of $M$ is required.

source.place: Tag 02KH, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology (2), degree zero and A′ → Frac(A′); elementary extraction of a basis from a spanning family

proof.text:
Choose $0\ne t\in\mathfrak m_s$. Its image in $A'$ is nonzero and belongs to the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_sA'$. Consequently $A'$ is an infinite domain: a finite domain is a field, whereas this maximal ideal is nonzero. The formula
$$\Phi(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)=\left(a_{0,K}+t\sum_{i=1}^e x_i h_{i,K},\ b_{0,K}+t\sum_{i=1}^e y_i h_{i,K}\right)$$
is an affine-space isomorphism $\mathbf A_K^{2e}\simeq V\times V$, since $t\ne0$ in $K$. Its inverse image of $W_n$ is nonempty open, so contains a nonempty basic open $D(P)$ for a nonzero polynomial $P\in K[X_1,\ldots,X_{2e}]$. There is a tuple in $(A')^{2e}$ where $P$ is nonzero. To see this without a rational-point assumption on $\kappa(s)$, induct on the number of variables: choose values in the infinite subset $A'\subset K$ making a nonzero coefficient polynomial nonzero, then avoid the finitely many roots of the remaining nonzero one-variable polynomial. For zero variables the assertion just says a nonzero constant is nonzero. Thus some $(\mathbf c,\mathbf d)\in(A')^{2e}$ maps into $W_n(K)$.

source.place: §3.4, printed p.606, lifting and Zariski-density paragraph; agent-written original-curve norm-section replacement (publisher PDF read online; local copy WANTED)

proof.text: Set $a=a_0+t\sum_i c_i h_i$ and $b=b_0+t\sum_i d_i h_i$ in $M$. The added terms restrict to zero on $Y_s$ because $t\in\mathfrak m_sA'$, so $(a_s,b_s)=(u^{\otimes r},v^{\otimes r})$. Step 3 proves the required special-fibre conclusions. The generic pair belongs to $W_n(K)$ by Step 6, so separating-pair-open proves all the required generic conclusions, including surjectivity and étaleness on a nonempty open. These are the actual norms in the statement: pullback commutes with each tensor factor and with its section, and then with the finite permutation and power comparisons defining $\mathcal N_G$. Explicitly, for $j=s,K$, restricting $\bigotimes_g g^*a$ gives $\bigotimes_g g_j^*(a_j)$ under $B|_{Y_j}=\bigotimes_g g_j^*L_j$, and the same holds for $b$. Thus the construction uses the original line bundle and original group action and imposes no characteristic restriction.
